audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 and 2+ items were both Urgot's although whys[0] calls Level 1 even and whys[6] and late both call the two-item stage a skill call.
audit.why: packet.levelChart reads Skill, Urgot x5, Skill, and this page's own prose already says the same at both ends.
audit.corrected: Skill at Level 1, Urgot Levels 2 through First item, Skill at two items.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was built on a 25% execute number and gave no cooldown for Abyssal Dive, the spike that actually matters.
audit.why: Riot's Fear Beyond Death text has no numeric threshold. Abyssal Dive is 21/20/19/18/17s and is his engage knockup — that long cooldown is the real trading window, and Devour can pull a target out of your execute range.
audit.corrected: Abyssal Dive is 21s at rank 1 — that is your window. At Level 6, Devour can swallow your target out of Fear Beyond Death's reach.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page uses Tahm Kench's retired kit: it calls Devour his W and names an ability 'Abyssal Voyage' as his R, in five places. It also credits gray-health regen to his passive.
audit.why: Riot's live kit is Tongue Lash (Q, 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s, 900 range, stuns only on the third An Acquired Taste stack), Abyssal Dive (W, 21/20/19/18/17s, knockup), Thick Skin (E, 3s, stores a percent of damage taken and converts it to a shield or out-of-combat heal), Devour (R). There is no Abyssal Voyage, and the stored-damage regen is Thick Skin, not the passive.
audit.corrected: Devour is his R and Abyssal Dive his W. Tongue Lash stuns only on the third stack, so never let him free-stack you. Thick Skin converts stored damage into a shield on a 3s cooldown — burst him in one window instead of chipping.

edits.before: - Tahm Kench Abyssal Dive: matchup-defining — His escape + shield. Shred when down. Track it before every engage. - Tahm Kench Tongue Lash: Lashes out to damage + slow (stuns at 3 passive stacks). Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Abyssal Dive: 21s at rank 1 — that is his knockup, not an escape. - Thick Skin: only 3s, converting stored damage into a shield. - Tongue Lash: 7s at 900 range, and it stuns only on the third stack.

edits.before: His escape + shield. Shred when down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Abyssal Dive is 21s at rank 1 — his knockup, and your longest safe window.

edits.before: Fear Beyond Death online — at 25% HP Tahm Kench is simply dead. Trade him to half, then the chain threat decides everything.
edits.after: Fear Beyond Death online — under its threshold he dies, but Devour can swallow your target out of range. Trade him to half.

edits.before: Late game your R is a pick machine: any frontliner dropped under 25% dies through everything. Anchor fights around the execute threat and W-shred whoever dives your carries. Tahm Kench carry threat: 6/10 — end the game before he cashes it.
edits.after: Late game your R is a pick machine: anyone dropped under its threshold dies through everything. Anchor fights around the execute threat and W-shred whoever dives your carries. Tahm Kench carry threat: 6/10 — end before he cashes it.

edits.before: You out-DPS Tahm Kench once you have Q Corrosive Charge and W Purge — his passive An Acquired Taste gray-health and W Devour dive threaten you, but in a straight trade your shred beats his tankiness before his stacks convert.
edits.after: You out-DPS Tahm Kench once you have Q Corrosive Charge and W Purge — but Thick Skin (E) turns stored damage into a shield on a 3s cooldown, so burst him inside one window rather than chipping, and never feed him three stacks.

edits.before: R Fear Beyond Death punishes a Tahm who steps up; just respect that his W Devour can eat an ally or self-peel, and his own R Abyssal Voyage is a roam threat, so ward and don't over-extend.
edits.after: Fear Beyond Death punishes a Tahm who steps up. Respect Devour (R): it eats an ally to save them, or you to take you out of the fight — and Abyssal Dive is a 21s gap-closer.

edits.before: Grievous Wounds cuts his passive gray-health regen and lifesteal; you keep the DPS lead as long as you dodge his Q Tongue Lash stun setup.
edits.after: Grievous Wounds cuts the Thick Skin heal and his Tongue Lash healing; you keep the DPS lead as long as you never give him three stacks.

edits.before: Tahm scales into a peel/pick tank whose Devour saves carries and Abyssal Voyage swings the map — his utility roughly matches your DPS teamfight value, making late-game a coin-flip.
edits.after: Tahm scales into a peel tank whose Devour (R) swallows a carry straight out of your execute range — his utility roughly matches your teamfight damage, so late-game comes down to who plays it better.

edits.before: Level 1-2 is a skill lane — Tahm's passive An Acquired Taste and W Devour make his all-in real, so if he lands Tongue Lash into a stun you can lose the trade; play the level and don't feed him stacks.
edits.after: Level 1-2 is a skill lane — An Acquired Taste needs three stacks before Tongue Lash stuns, so every lash he lands is a step toward losing the trade. Do not let him free-stack you off the wave.

edits.before: Late-game evens out into a skill matchup — Tahm's Devour peel and Abyssal Voyage roams give him real teamfight utility that trades off against your DPS, so the win goes to whoever executes better.
edits.after: Late-game evens out into a skill matchup — Devour (R) peels a carry straight out of your R threat and Abyssal Dive re-engages, so his utility trades off against your damage and execution decides it.

edits.before: Roam with Abyssal Voyage to swing other lanes
edits.after: Dive in with Abyssal Dive to start the fight
